summary: A set of mailing lists for sending network documents on paper. List A is for sites distributing their own documents to network liaisons, and lists B and C are used by the Network Information Center for other participants and for station agents. It carries names, organizations and addresses of recipients. It was replaced by RFC 363.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 329 provides three postal mailing lists for network documents: one for site liaisons, one for other participants, and one for NIC station agents. It replaced RFC 303 and was later replaced by RFC 363.

subtitle: Three postal mailing lists for distributing network documents in May 1972

tldr.problem: Network sites, participants and station agents needed updated mailing lists for distributing documents.
tldr.mechanism: Sites use List A to send their own documents to liaisons; the NIC uses Lists B and C for non-site participants and station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 329 replaced RFC 303 and was later replaced by RFC 363.

facts.label: Station-agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week or more often when quantity warrants

sections.title: The Three Mailing Lists
sections.content:
RFC 329 lists recipients for distributing network documents. Sites use List A to send their own documents to liaisons as quickly as possible; all mail other than local mail should go by air mail.

The NIC uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site network participants and station agents. RFC 329 says it obsoletes RFC 303.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites use List A to get their documents to liaisons. The NIC uses Lists B and C to reach other participants and station agents.

sections.title: Liaisons and Participants
sections.content:
List A includes network liaisons and others who receive initial distribution of RFCs, whether sent by the NIC or by sites. They also receive selected catalogs and other formal NIC documents.

List B identifies network participants who receive formal documents from the NIC. The lists provide names and postal addresses; this document includes contact information for the listed recipients.
sections.plainLanguage: List A is for initial RFC recipients. List B is for other participants who receive formal NIC documents.

sections.title: Station Agents and Successor
sections.content:
List C names NIC station agents. They receive copies of documents distributed to liaisons and documents sent as part of a station collection. The NIC mails to station agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.

The unit metadata records RFC 363 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 329.
sections.plainLanguage: List C identifies station agents who receive copies and station collections. RFC 363 later replaced this mailing list.
